newsitem.title: USA: High Court justice allows stay of telecom rules.
newsitem.headline: High Court justice allows stay of telecom rules.

text.p: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas refused Thursday to reinstate landmark federal rules aimed at prying open the nation's $100 billion local telephone market to full-fledged competition.

Thomas let stand a U.S. appeals court order suspending key parts of the Federal Communications Commission's "interconnection" rules. The FCC, long-distance giants AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp., and other phone companies had asked Thomas to restore the rules, but he rejected the request.

The appeals court, based in St. Louis, issued a "stay" on Oct. 15 while it considers a challenge to the rules, which spell out how long-distance carriers, cable-TV operators and others can link up to the local phone market under the new telecommunications law. Oral arguments are set for January.

GTE Corp., the Baby Bell phone companies, other local carriers and state regulators want to overturn the rules, saying the FCC overstepped its authority and usurped state powers to issue policies on pricing and other matters. Local companies and state regulators had requested the stay.
But the FCC and the long-distance companies told the high court the stay would hurt consumers by delaying the introduction of competition in the local market.
Thomas refused to lift the stay without any comment or explanation. The FCC and the long-distance companies could ask another Supreme Court justice to lift the stay.
The FCC rules, adopted in August, are intended to serve as a guide to negotiations between local phone companies and new rivals seeking to enter the local market.
